problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+1)-2xy,\,y(0)=-2
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $Δx=3.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Determining a General Update Formula for the Trapezoidal Method
examples.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
y' = 3x^2 - 2y, \qquad y(3) = -1
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $\Delta x = 4.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, $y_\text{new},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value $x_\text{new}.$
examples.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
y' = f(x,y), \qquad y(a) = c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $\Delta x$ is given by

$$
\Delta y = \dfrac12(y' + y'_\text{new}) \cdot \Delta x,
$$

with $y'_\text{new} = f(x_\text{new}, y_\text{new})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $\Delta y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3{x}^{2}-2y+(3({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-2{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 4 \\  & =6{x}^{2}+6{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-4y-4{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into $y_\text{new} = y + \Delta y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+6{x}^{2}+6{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}-4y-4{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =6{x}^{2}+6({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3y-4{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for the general formula for $y_\text{new}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}_{\text{new}} & =6{x}^{2}+6({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3y \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{5}(6{x}^{2}+6({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}-3y)\end{aligned}
$$
